Subject: Proposed DPA redlines + subprocessor exception request

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. Attached is a marked-up copy of your standard DPA (Acme_DPA_redline_20260210.pdf). There are three items we need clarification on and, if possible, an exception:

1) Analytics subprocessors: we see a clause that lists general analytics providers. Acme needs an explicit carveout to allow our processor to route telemetry to our analytics vendor (MixSight) for fraud detection. Can Redwood confirm which analytics subprocessors you currently use and whether you can accept a customer-specific exception?

2) Data-use restrictions: the redline requests that Redwood not use customer telemetry for model improvements. We need to understand retention windows and whether aggregated telemetry is used to tune routing/optimizer features.

3) Audit evidence: our security team may request SOC2 artifacts and logs showing request-level routing for a short period as part of procurement. Is that available under an NDA?

We attached a short summary of our redline comments. Please let me know if you need anything else from procurement/legal. We are aiming to get DPA signed before our internal fiscal review on Feb 26.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical notes from Product/Platform regarding the questions: 

1) Analytics subprocessors: Redwood does not currently route customer request/telemetry to third-party analytics by default. We run an internal telemetry pipeline (Redwood Telemetry) that collects anonymized metrics for platform health. Customers can provision an outbound integration (webhook or S3 export) that pushes selected telemetry fields to a customer-owned analytics endpoint; that export is under customer control and does not require Redwood to add a third-party subprocessor on their behalf.

2) Data-use/retention: By default we retain request-level logs for 90 days for debugging and billing reconciliation. Aggregated, non-identifying stats are used to improve system-level performance (e.g., autoscaling heuristics) but not to retrain customer-visible models. If Acme requires a stricter retention window or opt-out from aggregated telemetry, we can support a 30-day retention carveout for the account and disable opt-in telemetry feeds.

3) Audit evidence: We can provide SOC2 Type II summary reports under an NDA. Request-level routing traces (redacted) and capacity routing logs can be exported for a short window (30 days) if procurement/security signs a data access playbook (we have a template).

Implication for the DPA: technically, the preferred approach is to keep Redwood as the processor and allow Acme to configure their own outbound exports to MixSight. If Acme insists that MixSight be listed as a Redwood subprocessor, that triggers legal review and procurement of contracts with that vendor, which will slow timelines.

Let me know if you want technical docs for the export fields — I can attach a data schema and minimal sample.

— Dev

Morgan — appreciate the clear asks. From Security's perspective: 

- We are comfortable with a customer-managed export approach (Dev described) provided Acme confirms that the export endpoint is under Acme control and that no credential sharing occurs. We would require a short annex in the DPA that documents the allowed outbound telemetry fields and states Redwood will not route raw request payloads to third-party analytics on Acme's behalf without explicit written approval.
- Retention: security is OK with 30-day account-level retention as a contractual option. Operationally, we would enable a retention flag for the tenant and update our retention policy enforcement.
- Evidence: SOC2 summary + redacted routing logs under NDA is acceptable. Laura — we'll need legal to add the NDA clause and the data-access playbook reference into the DPA.

If Acme will accept those guardrails (export integration + 30-day retention + NDA for deeper logs), Security can sign off and Product can implement the retention flag.

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security | Redwood Inference

Morgan — following internal review, here is the proposed path forward and the language we can accept in the DPA: 

1) Subprocessor / analytics: We will not add MixSight or similar as a Redwood-managed subprocessor. Instead, Redwood will document and support a customer-managed outbound export (webhook or S3) that pushes a limited telemetry schema to Acme-owned analytics. The DPA will include an annex stating: 
   - Redwood will not route raw request payloads to customer analytics vendors on behalf of the customer without written approval.
   - Supported fields for the export are: request_id, timestamp, model_id, response_latency_ms, token_count, error_code. (Full schema shared in drive link.)

2) Data-use and retention: Redwood agrees to a 30-day retention option for Acme (contractual). Aggregated, anonymized metrics used for platform performance will be disabled for this account unless Acme explicitly opts in.

3) Audit evidence: We will provide SOC2 Type II summary under NDA and can provide redacted routing logs for a 30-day window via our data-access playbook. Laura — please add the NDA and playbook references and produce a redline patch for the DPA.

If that works, we can deliver the DPA redline (with annex) by EOD Friday Feb 13 so your procurement team has time before Feb 26. Please confirm acceptance of the approach or list items that must be changed.

Thanks — Connor
